[[zh:水若酢神社]][[ja:水若酢神社]] {{Short description|Shrine in Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Mizuwakasu-jinja shaden.JPG | deity = Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto | name = Mizuwakasu Shrine | map_type = Japan | map_caption = Mizuwakasu Shrine in Japan | coordinates = {{coord|36|16|51.57|N|133|14|57.19|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | location = [[Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima]], [[Oki District, Shimane|Oki District]], [[Shimane Prefecture]] | website = {{official|https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_mizuwakasu.html}} |name = Mizuwakasu Shrine |image = [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja shaden.JPG|270px]]
main hall (left, National Important Cultural Property) and Worship Hall |location = 723 Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]] |coordinates = {{Coord|36|16|48.78|N|133|14|56.54|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} |deity = Mizuwakasu no Mikoto |shrine_rank = [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha (Grand Shrine)]] of the [[Engishiki]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]], Beppyo Shrine |founded = (One tradition) during the reign of Emperor Sujin (10th Emperor), (Another tradition) during the reign of Emperor Nintoku (16th Emperor) |main_hall_style = [[Oki-zukuri]] |annual_festival = May 3 |shinto_rituals = Sairei Furyu (festival procession) every other year on May 3 |map = {{location map|Japan Shimane Prefecture|label=Mizuwakasu Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, ''Mizuwakasu-jinja'') is a Japanese [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima]], [[Oki District, Shimane|Oki District]], [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a ''[[Myojin Taisha]]''. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] [[Oki Province]] or the highest ranked shrine in the province.{{Cite web |title=Mizuwakasu Shrine {{!}} List of Geopark Sites and Treasures |url=https://www.oki-geopark.jp/en/geopark-sites-features-list/2694/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Oki Islands UNESCO Global Geopark |language=en-US}} It is ranked as a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a special shrine by the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The crest of the shrine has a chrysanthemum symbol.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-28 |title=水若酢神社（Mizuwakasu Shrine） - shrine-heritager |url=https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528184043/https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |archive-date=2023-05-28 }} It enshrines the deity Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto. This deity is linked to land development in Oki Province and sea protection.{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JSMvAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Shinto shrines and festivals |date=1958 |publisher=Association of Shinto Shrines, Kokugakuin University, Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics |language=ja}} == Overview == [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ichinotorii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii Gate}}]] '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, Mizuwakasu Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a [[Myōjin Taisha]] (Grand Shrine) of the [[Engishiki]], the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], and a former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine's crest (kamon) is "Chrysanthemum" . == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following three deities Shrine history documentation.{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}: ; Main deity :* '''Mizuwakasu no Mikoto''' (水若酢命) ; Auxiliary Deities :* Nakagoto no Mikoto (中言命, Nakagoto Kami) :* Suzu no Gozen (鈴御前) === About the Deities === [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|thumb|240px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine|ja|玉若酢命神社}} (Okinoshima-cho, Shimane)}}{{small|The Sōja (provincial shrine) of Oki Province. The connection between "Tamawakasu no Mikoto" and "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto" is noted.}}]] The deity's name in the [[Engishiki]] is recorded as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine." Although Mizuwakasu no Mikoto does not appear in major texts like the [[Kojiki]] or [[Nihon Shoki]], its origins are unclear due to the loss of historical documents in fires during the Middle Ages{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The meaning of "Mizu" can be interpreted as "water" or "auspicious," and "Wakasu" is also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The connection between this shrine and the nearby Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine is also noted{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The origins of the auxiliary deities Nakagoto no Mikoto and Suzu no Gozen are also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. The traditional text "Imijuyuraki" mentions these deities{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. == History == === Founding === Most of the ancient documents regarding the shrine's history were lost during the Middle Ages. According to the "Oki Chronicles" (1688), the deity appeared from the sea during the reign of Emperor Sujin and moved to its current location following the white doves{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. Another document from 1795 mentions that the deity was enshrined during the reign of Emperor Nintoku{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. According to local tradition, the deity moved several times before settling in its current location in Koori village during the Edo period{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=57-68}}. The current site is thought to have been the ancient district office of the Oki Province, evidenced by the large-scale kofun (tumuli) in the area{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. === Historical Summary === ==== Ancient Period ==== In the [[Shoku Nihongi]] (842 AD), it is recorded that the shrine, along with two others, was granted official status{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. In the [[Engishiki]] (927 AD), the shrine is listed as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine, Myōjin Taisha"{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The area is identified as Kawauchi-go in the Onji District, based on the names in the [[Wamyō Ruijushō]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. There are no records of the shrine from the mid-Heian to the early 15th century{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. ==== Medieval Period ==== The first medieval reference is from 1429, noting the shrine as the "Grand Shrine of Oki"{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. It is noted as the Ichinomiya of Oki Province from 1530{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}The Ichinomiya of Oki Province is sometimes identified as Yurahime Shrine, based on a note in the [[Dainihonkok Ichinomiya-ki]], but this is disputed by scholars{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}.. In the medieval period, the Oki Province was ruled by the Oki clan, leading to conflicts and the fall of the shrine's head priests{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. ==== Early Modern Period ==== In the Edo period, the shrine was relocated in 1676 after a flood and rebuilt at its current location in 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The main hall, built in 1795, is a designated Important Cultural Property{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. During the late Edo period, the shrine was involved in political movements, including the Sonnō Jōi (Revere the Emperor, Expel the Barbarians) movement{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. ==== Modern Period ==== After the [[Meiji Restoration]], the shrine was designated as a Kokuhei Chūsha in 1871 and later registered as a Beppyo Shrine{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. === Shrine ranking === * Senior Third rank (Engishiki) - Listed as "Mizuwakasu Myōjin." == History == According to legend, the deity rose from the sea, off the shore of Igo, crossed Mt. Ōmine and entered the former Goka Village. The shrine might date back to the Kofun Period. This was during [[Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suijin]] or [[Emperor Nintoku]]'s reign. In the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]], it was listed as a [[Myojin Taisha]] in 927.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QmdRAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Engi-shiki; Procedures of the Engi Era: Books VI-X|date=1972|publisher=Sophia University|language=en}} The shrine is important in Oki Province. It guards the [[Sea of Japan]]. It appears in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', a historical text. The ''Inshū Shicho Gakki'', from the [[Edo Period]], mentions it. The {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|sv}} names it as Mizuwakasu Myojin Oki Ichinomiya Shrine. The present [[Honden]] was made in [[1795]]. It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Business Japan|date=July 1988|publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun|language=en}} == Architecture == The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''. {{Infobox Chinese | kanji = 水若酢神社 | romaji = Mizuwakasu jinja | hiragana = みずわかすじんじゃ }} == Cultural Status == The shrine is designated as an [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government. == festivals == The grand festival is held on May 3 in odd-numbered years. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine has been located at its current site since 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. A white heron is said to have guided the deity to the present location, and a sacred pine tree called "Myōjin no Matsu" grew near the second torii gate until it died in 1971{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}. === Shrine Buildings === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, built in 1795, is an example of the [[Oki-zukuri]] style, unique to the region. The building is designated as an Important Cultural Property, along with associated documents{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. The worship hall, built in 1912, features a plaque inscribed with "First Shrine of Oki Province" from 1772{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. The gate was built in 1811{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. Other examples of Oki-zukuri include the main halls of [[Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine]] and [[Ise no Mikoto Shrine]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. File:Mizuwakasu-jinja suizhin-mon.jpg|Zuijin Gate File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ninotorii.jpg|Second Torii Gate === Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja kofun-1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumulus 1 Stone Chamber}}]] The shrine grounds contain several kofun (tumuli) from the Kofun period, known as the Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Only two tumuli remain today: :; Tumulus 1 :: Located east of the shrine buildings. The burial facility is a horizontal stone chamber with a total length of about 11 meters, the largest in the Oki Islands. Artifacts such as iron products and beads have been found{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. :; Tumulus 2 :: Located behind the shrine buildings. The details are unknown{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. == festivals == Major festivals at Mizuwakasu Shrine include{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=140-153}}: * New Year's Day festival (January 1) * Praying for Good Harvest (February 17) * '''festival''' (May 3) *: Known for the Sairei Furyu, a festival procession held every other year (even-numbered years). Events include the Yama-biki (Pulling the Mountain) ceremony, a procession of a decorated float called "Hōraisan," and various performances such as kagura, horseback archery, and dances. The festival is one of the "Three Great festivals of Oki" and is a designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. * Mid-year festival (June 16) * Harvest festival (November 3) * Gozasara festival (November 6) * Gozairi festival (December 6) * Year-End festival (December 31) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * main hall (with 8 wooden plaques and 6 construction documents) (Architecture) - Built in 1795. Designated on January 21, 1992{{Cultural Heritage Database|102|2991|Mizuwakasu Shrine main hall}}. === Shimane Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Intangible Folk Cultural Property ** Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu - Designated on March 30, 1973[http://www.town.okinoshima.shimane.jp/www/contents/1001000000257/index.html Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties (Intangible Cultural Properties) > Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu] (Okinoshima Town Education Committee).. == location == '''location''' * 723 Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]] '''Access''' * From [[Saigo Port]], take the [[Oki Ichibata Bus]] to "Mizuwakasu Shrine-mae" bus stop (about 40 minutes) - Very few buses operate. '''Surroundings''' * [[Oki Folk Museum]] * Goka Sozokan == Others == === Documentary === * [[NHK Special]] "Netsusen! Oki Tetsuya Sumo" (December 23, 1983, [[NHK General TV]]){{Cite web|url=https://www.nhk.jp/p/ts/DN23LL75QJ/episode/te/XWKNWX9R5P/ |title=Netsusen! Oki Tetsuya Sumo |date=1983-12-23 |publisher=NHK |archiveurl=https://archive.ph/nDI9N |archivedate=2021-07-10 |accessdate=2021-07-17}}. == See also == * {{Ill|Yurahime Shrine|simple|4=ja|5=由良比女神社|6=zh|7=由良比女神社}} == References == {{reflist|2}} == Further Reading == * Shrine history documentation * On-site information boards * Mizuwakasu Shrine edited books ** {{Cite According to local tradition, the deity moved several times before settling in its current location in Koori village during the Edo period{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=57-68}}. The current site is thought to have been the ancient district office of the Oki Province, evidenced by the large-scale kofun (tumuli) in the area{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. === Historical Summary === ==== Ancient Period ==== In the [[Shoku Nihongi]] (842 AD), it is recorded that the shrine, along with two others, was granted official status{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. In the [[Engishiki]] (927 AD), the shrine is listed as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine, Myōjin Taisha"{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The area is identified as Kawauchi-go in the Onji District, based on the names in the [[Wamyō Ruijushō]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. There are no records of the shrine from the mid-Heian to the early 15th century{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. ==== Medieval Period ==== The first medieval reference is from 1429, noting the shrine as the "Grand Shrine of Oki"{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. It is noted as the Ichinomiya of Oki Province from 1530{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}The Ichinomiya of Oki Province is sometimes identified as Yurahime Shrine, based on a note in the [[Dainihonkok Ichinomiya-ki]], but this is disputed by scholars{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}.. In the medieval period, the Oki Province was ruled by the Oki clan, leading to conflicts and the fall of the shrine's head priests{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. ==== Early Modern Period ==== In the Edo period, the shrine was relocated in 1676 after a flood and rebuilt at its current location in 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The main hall, built in 1795, is a designated Important Cultural Property{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. During the late Edo period, the shrine was involved in political movements, including the Sonnō Jōi (Revere the Emperor, Expel the Barbarians) movement{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. ==== Modern Period ==== After the [[Meiji Restoration]], the shrine was designated as a Kokuhei Chūsha in 1871 and later registered as a Beppyo Shrine{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. === Shrine ranking === * Senior Third rank (Engishiki) - Listed as "Mizuwakasu Myōjin." == History == According to legend, the deity rose from the sea, off the shore of Igo, crossed Mt. Ōmine and entered the former Goka Village. The shrine might date back to the Kofun Period. This was during [[Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suijin]] or [[Emperor Nintoku]]'s reign. In the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]], it was listed as a [[Myojin Taisha]] in 927.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QmdRAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Engi-shiki; Procedures of the Engi Era: Books VI-X|date=1972|publisher=Sophia University|language=en}} The shrine is important in Oki Province. It guards the [[Sea of Japan]]. It appears in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', a historical text. The ''Inshū Shicho Gakki'', from the [[Edo Period]], mentions it. The {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|sv}} names it as Mizuwakasu Myojin Oki Ichinomiya Shrine. The present [[Honden]] was made in [[1795]]. It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Business Japan|date=July 1988|publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun|language=en}} == Architecture == The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''. {{Infobox Chinese | kanji = 水若酢神社 | romaji = Mizuwakasu jinja | hiragana = みずわかすじんじゃ }} == Cultural Status == The shrine is designated as an [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government. == festivals == The grand festival is held on May 3 in odd-numbered years. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine has been located at its current site since 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. A white heron is said to have guided the deity to the present location, and a sacred pine tree called "Myōjin no Matsu" grew near the second torii gate until it died in 1971{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}. === Shrine Buildings === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, built in 1795, is an example of the [[Oki-zukuri]] style, unique to the region. The building is designated as an Important Cultural Property, along with associated documents{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. The worship hall, built in 1912, features a plaque inscribed with "First Shrine of Oki Province" from 1772{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. The gate was built in 1811{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. Other examples of Oki-zukuri include the main halls of [[Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine]] and [[Ise no Mikoto Shrine]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. File:Mizuwakasu-jinja suizhin-mon.jpg|Zuijin Gate File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ninotorii.jpg|Second Torii Gate === Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja kofun-1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumulus 1 Stone Chamber}}]] The shrine grounds contain several kofun (tumuli) from the Kofun period, known as the Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Only two tumuli remain today: :; Tumulus 1 :: Located east of the shrine buildings. The burial facility is a horizontal stone chamber with a total length of about 11 meters, the largest in the Oki Islands. Artifacts such as iron products and beads have been found{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. :; Tumulus 2 :: Located behind the shrine buildings. The details are unknown{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. == festivals == Major festivals at Mizuwakasu Shrine include{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=140-153}}: * New Year's Day festival (January 1) * Praying for Good Harvest (February 17) * '''festival''' (May 3) *: Known for the Sairei Furyu, a festival procession held every other year (even-numbered years). Events include the Yama-biki (Pulling the Mountain) ceremony, a procession of a decorated float called "Hōraisan," and various performances such as kagura, horseback archery, and dances. The festival is one of the "Three Great festivals of Oki" and is a designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. * Mid-year festival (June 16) * Harvest festival (November 3) * Gozasara festival (November 6) * Gozairi festival (December 6) * Year-End festival (December 31) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * main hall (with 8 wooden plaques and 6 construction documents) (Architecture) - Built in 1795. Designated on January 21, 1992{{Cultural Heritage Database|102|2991|Mizuwakasu Shrine main hall}}. === Shimane Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Intangible Folk Cultural Property ** Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu - Designated on March 30, 1973[http://www.town.okinoshima.shimane.jp/www/contents/1001000000257/index.html Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties (Intangible Cultural Properties) > Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu] (Okinoshima Town Education Committee).. == location == '''location''' * 723 Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]] '''Access''' * From [[Saigo Port]], take the [[Oki Ichibata Bus]] to "Mizuwakasu Shrine-mae" bus stop (about 40 minutes) - Very few buses operate. Oki Tetsuya Sumo |date=1983-12-23 |publisher=NHK |archiveurl=https://archive.ph/nDI9N |archivedate=2021-07-10 |accessdate=2021-07-17}}. == See also == * {{Ill|Yurahime main hall (left, National Important Cultural Property) and Worship Hall |location = 723 Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]] |coordinates = {{Coord|36|16|48.78|N|133|14|56.54|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} |deity = Mizuwakasu no Mikoto |shrine_rank = [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha (Grand Shrine)]] of the [[Engishiki]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]], Beppyo Shrine |founded = (One tradition) during the reign of Emperor Sujin (10th Emperor), (Another tradition) during the reign of Emperor Nintoku (16th Emperor) |main_hall_style = [[Oki-zukuri]] |annual_festival = May 3 |shinto_rituals = Sairei Furyu (festival procession) every other year on May 3 |map = {{location map|Japan Shimane Prefecture|label=Mizuwakasu Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, ''Mizuwakasu-jinja'') is a Japanese [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima]], [[Oki District, Shimane|Oki District]], [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a ''[[Myojin Taisha]]''. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] [[Oki Province]] or the highest ranked shrine in the province.{{Cite web |title=Mizuwakasu Shrine {{!}} List of Geopark Sites and Treasures |url=https://www.oki-geopark.jp/en/geopark-sites-features-list/2694/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Oki Islands UNESCO Global Geopark |language=en-US}} It is ranked as a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a special shrine by the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The crest of the shrine has a chrysanthemum symbol.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-28 |title=水若酢神社（Mizuwakasu Shrine） - shrine-heritager |url=https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528184043/https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |archive-date=2023-05-28 }} It enshrines the deity Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto. This deity is linked to land development in Oki Province and sea protection.{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JSMvAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Shinto shrines and festivals |date=1958 |publisher=Association of Shinto Shrines, Kokugakuin University, Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics |language=ja}} == Overview == [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ichinotorii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii Gate}}]] '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, Mizuwakasu Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a [[Myōjin Taisha]] (Grand Shrine) of the [[Engishiki]], the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], and a former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine's crest (kamon) is "Chrysanthemum" . == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following three deities Shrine history documentation.{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}: ; Main deity :* '''Mizuwakasu no Mikoto''' (水若酢命) ; Auxiliary Deities :* Nakagoto no Mikoto (中言命, Nakagoto Kami) :* Suzu no Gozen (鈴御前) === About the Deities === [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|thumb|240px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine|ja|玉若酢命神社}} (Okinoshima-cho, Shimane)}}{{small|The Sōja (provincial shrine) of Oki Province. The connection between "Tamawakasu no Mikoto" and "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto" is noted.}}]] The deity's name in the [[Engishiki]] is recorded as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine." The meaning of "Mizu" can be interpreted as "water" or "auspicious," and "Wakasu" is also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The connection between this shrine and the nearby Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine is also noted{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The origins of the auxiliary deities Nakagoto no Mikoto and Suzu no Gozen are also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. Only two tumuli remain today: :; Tumulus 1 :: Located east of the shrine buildings. The burial facility is a horizontal stone chamber with a total length of about 11 meters, the largest in the Oki Islands. Artifacts such as iron products and beads have been found{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. :; Tumulus 2 :: Located behind the shrine buildings. The details are unknown{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. == festivals == Major festivals at Mizuwakasu Shrine include{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=140-153}}: * New Year's Day festival (January 1) * Praying for Good Harvest (February 17) * '''festival''' (May 3) *: Known for the Sairei Furyu, a festival procession held every other year (even-numbered years). Events include the Yama-biki (Pulling the Mountain) ceremony, a procession of a decorated float called "Hōraisan," and various performances such as kagura, horseback archery, and dances. The festival is one of the "Three Great festivals of Oki" and is a designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. * Mid-year festival (June 16) * Harvest festival (November 3) * Gozasara festival (November 6) * Gozairi festival (December 6) * Year-End festival (December 31) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * main hall (with 8 wooden plaques and 6 construction documents) (Architecture) - Built in 1795. Designated on January 21, 1992{{Cultural Heritage Database|102|2991|Mizuwakasu Shrine main hall}}. === Shimane Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Intangible Folk Cultural Property ** Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu - Designated on March 30, 1973[http://www.town.okinoshima.shimane.jp/www/contents/1001000000257/index.html Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties (Intangible Cultural Properties) > Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu] (Okinoshima Town Education Committee).. == location == '''location''' * 723 Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]] '''Access''' * From [[Saigo Port]], take the [[Oki Ichibata Bus]] to "Mizuwakasu Shrine-mae" bus stop (about 40 minutes) - Very few buses operate. '''水若酢神社'''（みずわかすじんじゃ）は、[[島根県]][[隠岐郡]][[隠岐の島町]]郡（こおり）にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）、[[隠岐国]][[一宮]]。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[国幣中社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。[[神紋]]は「菊」。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の3柱神社由緒書。{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=69-90}}。 ; 主祭神 :* '''水若酢命'''（みずわかすのみこと） ; 配祀神 :* 中言命（なかごとのみこと、中言神） :* 鈴御前（すずのごぜん） === 祭神について === [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|thumb|240px|right|{{center|[[玉若酢命神社]]（隠岐の島町下西）}}{{small|隠岐国[[総社]]。祭神の「玉若酢命」について「水若酢命」との関連性が指摘される。}}]] [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]での祭神の記載は1座。現在は社名を「水若酢神社」とするが、同帳の記載では「水若酢命神社」とあり、祭神が「水若酢命」であることが知られる。この神は『[[古事記]]』・『[[日本書紀]]』に記載が見えない地方神であるが{{Sfn|水若酢神社（神々）|2000年}}{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=440}}、由緒を伝える水若酢神社の史料は兵火等で失われているため、詳らかでない{{Sfn|水若酢神社（日本大百科全書）}}。神名の「ミズワカス」のうち、「ミズ」の字義は文字通りの「水」の意とする説や美称の「瑞」の意とする説があって明らかでなく、「ワカス」の字義も明らかでない{{Sfn|水若酢神社（神々）|2000年}}。『延喜式』神名帳では隠岐国に「[[玉若酢命神社]]」の記載も見え、同社の社名と水若酢神社との関連性も指摘される{{Sfn|水若酢神社（神々）|2000年}}。 他の祭神である中言命・鈴御前の由緒も詳らかでない{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=69-90}}。確かな史料ではないが、古伝書『伊未自由来記』には美豆別主命（水若酢命）・奈賀命（中言命）・須津姫（鈴御前）の伝承が記されている{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=69-90}}。なお『[[隠州視聴合記]]』では祭神を[[崇神天皇]]（第10代天皇）とするが、これは崇神天皇の時代に神が顕現したとする由緒を取り違えたものとされている{{Sfn|水若酢命神社（式内社）|1983年}}。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === 水若酢神社では由緒に関する古文書のほとんどが[[中世]]期に兵火等で失われているため、創建は詳らかでない。『隠州記』（[[貞享]]5年（[[1688年]]）著）の伝承では、[[崇神天皇]]（第10代）の時に神が海中から伊後の地に上がり、白鳩2羽に乗って遷座したとする{{Sfn|水若酢命神社（式内社）|1983年}}。また[[寛政]]7年（[[1795年]]）の文書では、[[仁徳天皇]]（第16代）の時に祭神が[[勧請]]されたとする{{Sfn|水若酢命神社（式内社）|1983年}}。 隠岐島の伝承では、白鳩ではなく白鷺によって神が伊後から捧羽山（ほうばやま、芳葉山）などを経て山田村（隠岐の島町山田）、一宮村宮原（隠岐の島町郡）と移り、さらに[[江戸時代]]の洪水の際に現社地の郡村犬町（隠岐の島町郡）に遷座したとする（一宮村宮原以前の遷座年は不詳）{{Sfn|水若酢命神社（式内社）|1983年}}{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=39-56}}{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=57-68}}。 現社地は「郡」という地名から[[隠岐国]][[穏地郡]]の[[郡家]]所在地と推測される地域で{{Sfn|水若酢神社（神々）|2000年}}、境内一帯では隠岐諸島最大級の[[横穴式石室]]を有する水若酢神社古墳群の分布も知られる{{Sfn|水若酢神社古墳群（平凡社）|1995年}}。 === 概史 === ==== 古代 ==== [[六国史|国史]]では、『[[続日本後紀]]』[[承和 (日本)|承和]]9年（[[842年]]）条において、由良比売命神（[[西ノ島]]の[[由良比女神社]]）・宇受加命神（[[中ノ島 (島根県)|中ノ島]]の[[宇受賀命神社]]）・水若酢命神（水若酢神社）の3社が[[官社]]に預かる旨が記されている{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では隠岐国穏地郡に「水若酢命神社 名神大」と記載され、[[名神大社]]に列している{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。『延喜式』臨時祭の名神祭条でも「水若酢命神社一座」とある。[[平安時代]]中期の『[[和名類聚抄|和名抄]]』に見える地名のうちでは、当地は穏地郡河内郷（かむちごう）に比定される「河内郷」 『日本歴史地名大系 33 島根県の地名』 平凡社、1995年。{{Sfn|水若酢命神社（式内社）|1983年}}。その後は[[15世紀]]まで当社のことを記す史料が見つかっておらず、変遷は不詳{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=440}}。 ==== 中世 ==== [[中世]]期の史料の初見は[[正長]]2年（[[1429年]]）の「久清書状写」で、「隠州大宮司社領」と見える{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=440}}。また[[享禄]]3年（[[1530年]]）の史料に「一宮造作」と見えるのを初見として、隠岐国では[[一宮]]の位置づけにあった{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=440}}隠岐国一宮については、『[[大日本国一宮記]]』の記載を基に[[由良比女神社]]（西ノ島町浦郷）に比定する説もある。ただし、『中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究』はその説について根拠に欠け実態にも沿わないとして否定的な見解を示しており、そのような説が浮上した要因として、『隠岐国神名帳』に見えるような中世期の水若酢神社の地位の低下を指摘する {{Harv|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=440}}。。ただし神官が「大宮司」を称したのは隠岐国で当社だけであることから、先の正長2年の文書をもって一宮の初見とする説もある{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=440}}。しかしながら『隠岐国神名帳』によれば、当社は「正三位 水若酢明神」として正三位の位置づけにあった一方、天健金草神社・[[玉若酢命神社]]は正一位の位置づけにあったことから、中世期には地位が低下し名目上の一宮であった可能性も指摘される{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=440}}。 中世の隠岐諸島では、隠岐国[[守護代]]である隠岐氏の伸長に伴って隠岐氏・在地勢力の間で対立が強まっており、[[享禄]]3年（[[1530年]]）の文書では「大宮司謀叛」のことがあって大宮司が代氏に代わったと見える（ただし検討が必要な史料とされる。代氏以前の大宮司は不明）{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。また『[[雲陽軍実記]]』や『[[陰徳太平記]]』にも、隠岐清政と在地武士との争いにより隠岐氏が島前・島後を支配するようになった旨が見えており、隠岐氏との争いの中で水若酢神社の大宮司が没落したのは事実とされる{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=440}}。[[天正]]5年（[[1577年]]）の文書では代民部助の一宮大宮司職への補任の旨が見え、大宮司職は続けて代氏によって継承されている{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。 ==== 近世 ==== [[江戸時代]]に入り、[[寛永]]15年（[[1638年]]）の文書では、[[慶長]]4年（[[1599年]]）の作分70石余および[[吉川氏]]時代の寄免分30石が山田村・郡村・苗代田村にある旨や、社領が10石である旨、大宮司が忌部正景である旨が見える{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。[[貞享]]5年（[[1688年]]）の『増補隠州記』では「一宮明神」について、一宮村にある旨と、社領10石である旨が記されている{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。一宮村での旧鎮座地は山田川・郡川の合流地付近とされ、[[寛文]]7年（[[1667年]]）の『[[隠州視聴合記]]』にも「一宮の神祠は田園の中に在り」と見える{{Sfn|水若酢命神社（式内社）|1983年}}{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=57-68}}。 [[延宝]]4年（[[1676年]]）には洪水で社殿が流失し、延宝6年（[[1678年]]）にそれまでの一宮村から郡村に遷座したとされる{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。[[寛政]]7年（[[1795年]]）には現在の本殿（国の[[重要文化財]]）が造営された{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。 江戸時代後期には、大宮司の忌部正興が『凶年蔵土穂』において[[松江藩]]政に対する批判を行なっている{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。また幕末期には、[[国学者]]の中西毅男が境内に私塾「膺懲館」を設けて[[尊皇攘夷]]を唱え{{Sfn|水若酢神社（日本大百科全書）}}、それが発展して忌部正弘が正義党を率いて[[隠岐騒動]]を指導している{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。 ==== 近代以降 ==== [[明治維新]]後、社号を「水若酢神社」と定めるとともに、[[明治]]4年（[[1871年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[国幣中社]]に列した{{Sfn|水若酢命神社（式内社）|1983年}}。 戦後は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に列している。 === 神階 === * 正三位 （『隠岐国神名帳』） - 表記は「水若酢明神」。 == 境内 == 現社地は、江戸時代前期の[[延宝]]6年（[[1678年]]）以来の鎮座とされる{{Sfn|水若酢神社（平凡社）|1995年}}。その際の鎮座地の選定は神獣の白鷺が当地の松に止まったことによるといい、境内の二の鳥居付近にはその「明神の松」が生育していたが、[[昭和]]46年（[[1971年]]）に枯死している{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=39-56}}。 === 社殿 === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿（国の重要文化財）}}]] 社殿のうち'''[[本殿]]'''は、江戸時代の[[寛政]]7年（[[1795年]]）の造営。[[身舎]]（もや）は[[切妻造]][[妻入]]で、桁行（側面）二間、梁間（正面）三間の大規模な建築になる。屋根は[[茅葺]]で、棟には[[千木・鰹木]]を置き、身舎前面には片流れ・栃葺の庇を付す。身舎内部は前一間を外陣、後一間を内陣とし、外陣・内陣とも畳敷きで、内陣奥に神体を納める厨子が据えられている。この本殿は「[[隠岐造]]（おきづくり）」と称される独特な神社建築様式で、その造営に係る棟札・普請文書もよく残されていることから、本殿および棟札・普請文書（附指定）は国の[[重要文化財]]に指定されている[http://www.town.okinoshima.shimane.jp/www/contents/1001000000248/index.html 国指定文化財 > 水若酢神社]（隠岐の島町教育委員会）。{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=91-103}}。 本殿前に建てられている拝殿は、[[大正]]元年（[[1912年]]）の造営{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=9-21}}。拝殿に掲げられる「隠岐州 第壹宮」銘の扁額は、[[明和]]9年（[[1772年]]）に幕府巡見使として当地に至った佐久間東川の書による{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=9-21}}。拝殿前の随神門は、[[文化 (元号)|文化]]8年（[[1811年]]）の造営になる{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=9-21}}。 なお、水若酢神社本殿と同様の隠岐造の建物は、[[玉若酢命神社]]本殿（隠岐の島町下西、[[寛政]]5年（[[1793年]]）造営、国の重要文化財）・[[伊勢命神社]]本殿（隠岐の島町久見、[[天保]]12年（[[1841年]]）造営、隠岐の島町指定文化財）などでも知られるほか、一間四方の小規模な隠岐造の社殿は隠岐諸島の各地に伝わる{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=91-103}}。 File:Mizuwakasu-jinja suizhin-mon.jpg|随神門 File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ninotorii.jpg|二の鳥居 === 水若酢神社古墳群 === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja kofun-1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|水若酢神社1号墳 石室}}]] 水若酢神社の境内一帯には'''水若酢神社古墳群'''（または姿だわ古墳群）と称される[[古墳時代]]後期の古墳群が分布する{{Sfn|水若酢神社古墳群（平凡社）|1995年}}。かつては数基の古墳があったというが、現在は次の2基のみを遺存する。 :; 1号墳 :: 社殿東方に位置する。現在では封土が失われており、墳形は不明。埋葬施設は[[横穴式石室]]で、現在は地表に露出するが、石室全長が約11メートルと隠岐諸島では最大級の規模になる。この石室内部では石棺2基のほか、鉄製品（太刀・鍬など）・勾玉などの副葬品が検出された。また、[[6世紀]]中頃-[[7世紀]]頃の土器も出土している{{Sfn|水若酢神社古墳群（平凡社）|1995年}}水若酢神社古墳群 説明板（隠岐の島町教育委員会設置）。。 :; 2号墳 :: 社殿裏に位置する。直径約20メートル、高さ2.5メートルの[[円墳]]と推定される。詳細は明らかでない{{Sfn|水若酢神社古墳群（平凡社）|1995年}}。 == 祭事 == 水若酢神社で年間に行われる主な祭事は次の通り{{Sfn|水若酢神社（学生社）|2005年|pp=140-153}}。 * 元旦祭 （1月1日） * 祈年祭 （2月17日） * '''例大祭''' （5月3日） *: かつては旧暦3月3日に斎行された。現在では特に隔年（西暦偶数年）に催される'''祭礼風流'''（さいれいふうりゅう）が知られる。この祭礼風流では、「蓬莱山」と呼ばれる山車を[[御旅所]]まで曳く「山曳き神事」や、御旅所で巫女舞・一番立・獅子舞・大楽・流鏑馬といった各種神事が催される。そのうち「山曳き神事」は、社殿流失に伴う再建時の用材曳きに由来するといわれる。この祭礼風流は「隠岐三大祭」の1つに数えられるほか、島根県指定無形民俗文化財に指定されている{{Sfn|水若酢命神社（式内社）|1983年}}水若酢神社祭礼風流 説明板（隠岐の島町教育委員会設置）。。 * 中祭 （6月16日） * 新嘗祭 （11月3日） * 御座更祭 （11月6日） * 御座入祭 （12月6日） * 除夜祭 （12月31日） == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 本殿（附 棟札8枚、普請文書6冊）（建造物） - 江戸時代後期、寛政7年（1795年）の造営。平成4年（1992年）1月21日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|102|2991|水若酢神社本殿}}。 === 島根県指定文化財 === * 無形民俗文化財 ** 水若酢神社祭礼風流 - 昭和48年（1973年）3月30日指定[http://www.town.okinoshima.shimane.jp/www/contents/1001000000257/index.html 県指定文化財（民俗文化財） > 水若酢神社祭礼風流]（隠岐の島町教育委員会）。。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[島根県]][[隠岐郡]][[隠岐の島町]]郡723 '''交通アクセス''' * [[西郷港]]から[[隠岐一畑交通|隠岐一畑バス]]で「水若酢神社前」バス停下車（乗車時間約40分） - 本数は僅少。 '''周辺''' * [[隠岐郷土館]] * 五箇創生館 == その他 == === ドキュメンタリー === * [[NHK特集]]「熱戦！隠岐 徹夜相撲」（1983年12月23日、[[NHK総合テレビジョン|NHK]]）{{Cite |accessdate=2021-07-17}} == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} === 注釈 === {{reflist|group="注"}} === 出典 === {{reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * 神社由緒書 * 境内説明板 * 水若酢神社編集書籍 ** {{Cite (昭和時代)|国史大辞典]]|publisher=[[吉川弘文館]]|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|水若酢神社（国史）}}}} ** {{Cite [[zh:水若酢神社]][[ja:水若酢神社]] {{Short description|Shrine in Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Mizuwakasu-jinja shaden.JPG | deity = Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto | name = Mizuwakasu Shrine | map_type = Japan | map_caption = Mizuwakasu Shrine in Japan | coordinates = {{coord|36|16|51.57|N|133|14|57.19|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | location = [[Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima]], [[Oki District, Shimane|Oki District]], [[Shimane Prefecture]] | website = {{official|https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_mizuwakasu.html}} |name = Mizuwakasu Shrine |image = [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja shaden.JPG|270px]]
main hall (left, National Important Cultural Property) and Worship Hall |location = 723 Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]] |coordinates = {{Coord|36|16|48.78|N|133|14|56.54|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} |deity = Mizuwakasu no Mikoto |shrine_rank = [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha (Grand Shrine)]] of the [[Engishiki]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]], Beppyo Shrine |founded = (One tradition) during the reign of Emperor Sujin (10th Emperor), (Another tradition) during the reign of Emperor Nintoku (16th Emperor) |main_hall_style = [[Oki-zukuri]] |annual_festival = May 3 |shinto_rituals = Sairei Furyu (festival procession) every other year on May 3 |map = {{location map|Japan Shimane Prefecture|label=Mizuwakasu Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, ''Mizuwakasu-jinja'') is a Japanese [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima]], [[Oki District, Shimane|Oki District]], [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a ''[[Myojin Taisha]]''. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] [[Oki Province]] or the highest ranked shrine in the province.{{Cite web |title=Mizuwakasu Shrine {{!}} List of Geopark Sites and Treasures |url=https://www.oki-geopark.jp/en/geopark-sites-features-list/2694/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Oki Islands UNESCO Global Geopark |language=en-US}} It is ranked as a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a special shrine by the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The crest of the shrine has a chrysanthemum symbol.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-28 |title=水若酢神社（Mizuwakasu Shrine） - shrine-heritager |url=https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528184043/https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |archive-date=2023-05-28 }} It enshrines the deity Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto. This deity is linked to land development in Oki Province and sea protection.{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JSMvAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Shinto shrines and festivals |date=1958 |publisher=Association of Shinto Shrines, Kokugakuin University, Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics |language=ja}} == Overview == [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ichinotorii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii Gate}}]] '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, Mizuwakasu Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a [[Myōjin Taisha]] (Grand Shrine) of the [[Engishiki]], the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], and a former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine's crest (kamon) is "Chrysanthemum" . == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following three deities Shrine history documentation.{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}: ; Main deity :* '''Mizuwakasu no Mikoto''' (水若酢命) ; Auxiliary Deities :* Nakagoto no Mikoto (中言命, Nakagoto Kami) :* Suzu no Gozen (鈴御前) === About the Deities === [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|thumb|240px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine|ja|玉若酢命神社}} (Okinoshima-cho, Shimane)}}{{small|The Sōja (provincial shrine) of Oki Province. The connection between "Tamawakasu no Mikoto" and "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto" is noted.}}]] The deity's name in the [[Engishiki]] is recorded as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine." Although Mizuwakasu no Mikoto does not appear in major texts like the [[Kojiki]] or [[Nihon Shoki]], its origins are unclear due to the loss of historical documents in fires during the Middle Ages{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The meaning of "Mizu" can be interpreted as "water" or "auspicious," and "Wakasu" is also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The connection between this shrine and the nearby Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine is also noted{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The origins of the auxiliary deities Nakagoto no Mikoto and Suzu no Gozen are also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. The traditional text "Imijuyuraki" mentions these deities{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. == History == === Founding === Most of the ancient documents regarding the shrine's history were lost during the Middle Ages. According to the "Oki Chronicles" (1688), the deity appeared from the sea during the reign of Emperor Sujin and moved to its current location following the white doves{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. Another document from 1795 mentions that the deity was enshrined during the reign of Emperor Nintoku{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. According to local tradition, the deity moved several times before settling in its current location in Koori village during the Edo period{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=57-68}}. The current site is thought to have been the ancient district office of the Oki Province, evidenced by the large-scale kofun (tumuli) in the area{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. === Historical Summary === ==== Ancient Period ==== In the [[Shoku Nihongi]] (842 AD), it is recorded that the shrine, along with two others, was granted official status{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. In the [[Engishiki]] (927 AD), the shrine is listed as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine, Myōjin Taisha"{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The area is identified as Kawauchi-go in the Onji District, based on the names in the [[Wamyō Ruijushō]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. There are no records of the shrine from the mid-Heian to the early 15th century{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. ==== Medieval Period ==== The first medieval reference is from 1429, noting the shrine as the "Grand Shrine of Oki"{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. It is noted as the Ichinomiya of Oki Province from 1530{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}The Ichinomiya of Oki Province is sometimes identified as Yurahime Shrine, based on a note in the [[Dainihonkok Ichinomiya-ki]], but this is disputed by scholars{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}.. In the medieval period, the Oki Province was ruled by the Oki clan, leading to conflicts and the fall of the shrine's head priests{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. ==== Early Modern Period ==== In the Edo period, the shrine was relocated in 1676 after a flood and rebuilt at its current location in 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The main hall, built in 1795, is a designated Important Cultural Property{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. During the late Edo period, the shrine was involved in political movements, including the Sonnō Jōi (Revere the Emperor, Expel the Barbarians) movement{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. ==== Modern Period ==== After the [[Meiji Restoration]], the shrine was designated as a Kokuhei Chūsha in 1871 and later registered as a Beppyo Shrine{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. === Shrine ranking === * Senior Third rank (Engishiki) - Listed as "Mizuwakasu Myōjin." == History == According to legend, the deity rose from the sea, off the shore of Igo, crossed Mt. Ōmine and entered the former Goka Village. The shrine might date back to the Kofun Period. This was during [[Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suijin]] or [[Emperor Nintoku]]'s reign. In the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]], it was listed as a [[Myojin Taisha]] in 927.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QmdRAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Engi-shiki; Procedures of the Engi Era: Books VI-X|date=1972|publisher=Sophia University|language=en}} The shrine is important in Oki Province. It guards the [[Sea of Japan]]. It appears in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', a historical text. The ''Inshū Shicho Gakki'', from the [[Edo Period]], mentions it. The {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|sv}} names it as Mizuwakasu Myojin Oki Ichinomiya Shrine. The present [[Honden]] was made in [[1795]]. It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Business Japan|date=July 1988|publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun|language=en}} == Architecture == The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''. {{Infobox Chinese | kanji = 水若酢神社 | romaji = Mizuwakasu jinja | hiragana = みずわかすじんじゃ }} == Cultural Status == The shrine is designated as an [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government. == festivals == The grand festival is held on May 3 in odd-numbered years. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine has been located at its current site since 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. A white heron is said to have guided the deity to the present location, and a sacred pine tree called "Myōjin no Matsu" grew near the second torii gate until it died in 1971{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}. === Shrine Buildings === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, built in 1795, is an example of the [[Oki-zukuri]] style, unique to the region. The building is designated as an Important Cultural Property, along with associated documents{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. The worship hall, built in 1912, features a plaque inscribed with "First Shrine of Oki Province" from 1772{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. The gate was built in 1811{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. Other examples of Oki-zukuri include the main halls of [[Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine]] and [[Ise no Mikoto Shrine]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. File:Mizuwakasu-jinja suizhin-mon.jpg|Zuijin Gate File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ninotorii.jpg|Second Torii Gate === Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja kofun-1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumulus 1 Stone Chamber}}]] The shrine grounds contain several kofun (tumuli) from the Kofun period, known as the Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Only two tumuli remain today: :; Tumulus 1 :: Located east of the shrine buildings. The burial facility is a horizontal stone chamber with a total length of about 11 meters, the largest in the Oki Islands. Artifacts such as iron products and beads have been found{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. :; Tumulus 2 :: Located behind the shrine buildings. The details are unknown{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. == festivals == Major festivals at Mizuwakasu Shrine include{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=140-153}}: * New Year's Day festival (January 1) * Praying for Good Harvest (February 17) * '''festival''' (May 3) *: Known for the Sairei Furyu, a festival procession held every other year (even-numbered years). Events include the Yama-biki (Pulling the Mountain) ceremony, a procession of a decorated float called "Hōraisan," and various performances such as kagura, horseback archery, and dances. [[zh:水若酢神社]][[ja:水若酢神社]] {{Short description|Shrine in Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Mizuwakasu-jinja shaden.JPG | deity = Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto | name = Mizuwakasu Shrine | map_type = Japan | map_caption = Mizuwakasu Shrine in Japan | coordinates = {{coord|36|16|51.57|N|133|14|57.19|E|region:JP|display=inline,title}} | location = [[Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima]], [[Oki District, Shimane|Oki District]], [[Shimane Prefecture]] | website = {{official|https://oki-dougo.info/data01/room/sroom/shrine/sroom_mizuwakasu.html}} |name = Mizuwakasu Shrine |image = [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja shaden.JPG|270px]]
main hall (left, National Important Cultural Property) and Worship Hall |location = 723 Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]] |coordinates = {{Coord|36|16|48.78|N|133|14|56.54|E|region:JP-32_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Mizuwakasu Shrine}} |deity = Mizuwakasu no Mikoto |shrine_rank = [[Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha (Grand Shrine)]] of the [[Engishiki]], [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]], Beppyo Shrine |founded = (One tradition) during the reign of Emperor Sujin (10th Emperor), (Another tradition) during the reign of Emperor Nintoku (16th Emperor) |main_hall_style = [[Oki-zukuri]] |annual_festival = May 3 |shinto_rituals = Sairei Furyu (festival procession) every other year on May 3 |map = {{location map|Japan Shimane Prefecture|label=Mizuwakasu Shrine|position=left|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, ''Mizuwakasu-jinja'') is a Japanese [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Okinoshima, Shimane|Okinoshima]], [[Oki District, Shimane|Oki District]], [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a ''[[Myojin Taisha]]''. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] [[Oki Province]] or the highest ranked shrine in the province.{{Cite web |title=Mizuwakasu Shrine {{!}} List of Geopark Sites and Treasures |url=https://www.oki-geopark.jp/en/geopark-sites-features-list/2694/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Oki Islands UNESCO Global Geopark |language=en-US}} It is ranked as a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a special shrine by the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The crest of the shrine has a chrysanthemum symbol.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-28 |title=水若酢神社（Mizuwakasu Shrine） - shrine-heritager |url=https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528184043/https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |archive-date=2023-05-28 }} It enshrines the deity Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto. This deity is linked to land development in Oki Province and sea protection.{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JSMvAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Shinto shrines and festivals |date=1958 |publisher=Association of Shinto Shrines, Kokugakuin University, Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics |language=ja}} == Overview == [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ichinotorii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii Gate}}]] '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, Mizuwakasu Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a [[Myōjin Taisha]] (Grand Shrine) of the [[Engishiki]], the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], and a former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine's crest (kamon) is "Chrysanthemum" . == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following three deities Shrine history documentation.{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}: ; Main deity :* '''Mizuwakasu no Mikoto''' (水若酢命) ; Auxiliary Deities :* Nakagoto no Mikoto (中言命, Nakagoto Kami) :* Suzu no Gozen (鈴御前) === About the Deities === [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|thumb|240px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine|ja|玉若酢命神社}} (Okinoshima-cho, Shimane)}}{{small|The Sōja (provincial shrine) of Oki Province. The connection between "Tamawakasu no Mikoto" and "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto" is noted.}}]] The deity's name in the [[Engishiki]] is recorded as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine." Although Mizuwakasu no Mikoto does not appear in major texts like the [[Kojiki]] or [[Nihon Shoki]], its origins are unclear due to the loss of historical documents in fires during the Middle Ages{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The meaning of "Mizu" can be interpreted as "water" or "auspicious," and "Wakasu" is also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The connection between this shrine and the nearby Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine is also noted{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The origins of the auxiliary deities Nakagoto no Mikoto and Suzu no Gozen are also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. The traditional text "Imijuyuraki" mentions these deities{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. == History == === Founding === Most of the ancient documents regarding the shrine's history were lost during the Middle Ages. According to the "Oki Chronicles" (1688), the deity appeared from the sea during the reign of Emperor Sujin and moved to its current location following the white doves{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. Another document from 1795 mentions that the deity was enshrined during the reign of Emperor Nintoku{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. According to local tradition, the deity moved several times before settling in its current location in Koori village during the Edo period{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=57-68}}. The current site is thought to have been the ancient district office of the Oki Province, evidenced by the large-scale kofun (tumuli) in the area{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. === Historical Summary === ==== Ancient Period ==== In the [[Shoku Nihongi]] (842 AD), it is recorded that the shrine, along with two others, was granted official status{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. In the [[Engishiki]] (927 AD), the shrine is listed as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine, Myōjin Taisha"{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The area is identified as Kawauchi-go in the Onji District, based on the names in the [[Wamyō Ruijushō]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. There are no records of the shrine from the mid-Heian to the early 15th century{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. ==== Medieval Period ==== The first medieval reference is from 1429, noting the shrine as the "Grand Shrine of Oki"{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. It is noted as the Ichinomiya of Oki Province from 1530{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}The Ichinomiya of Oki Province is sometimes identified as Yurahime Shrine, based on a note in the [[Dainihonkok Ichinomiya-ki]], but this is disputed by scholars{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}.. In the medieval period, the Oki Province was ruled by the Oki clan, leading to conflicts and the fall of the shrine's head priests{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. ==== Early Modern Period ==== In the Edo period, the shrine was relocated in 1676 after a flood and rebuilt at its current location in 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The main hall, built in 1795, is a designated Important Cultural Property{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. During the late Edo period, the shrine was involved in political movements, including the Sonnō Jōi (Revere the Emperor, Expel the Barbarians) movement{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. ==== Modern Period ==== After the [[Meiji Restoration]], the shrine was designated as a Kokuhei Chūsha in 1871 and later registered as a Beppyo Shrine{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. === Shrine ranking === * Senior Third rank (Engishiki) - Listed as "Mizuwakasu Myōjin." == History == According to legend, the deity rose from the sea, off the shore of Igo, crossed Mt. Ōmine and entered the former Goka Village. The shrine might date back to the Kofun Period. This was during [[Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suijin]] or [[Emperor Nintoku]]'s reign. In the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]], it was listed as a [[Myojin Taisha]] in 927.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QmdRAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Engi-shiki; Procedures of the Engi Era: Books VI-X|date=1972|publisher=Sophia University|language=en}} The shrine is important in Oki Province. It guards the [[Sea of Japan]]. It appears in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', a historical text. The ''Inshū Shicho Gakki'', from the [[Edo Period]], mentions it. The {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|sv}} names it as Mizuwakasu Myojin Oki Ichinomiya Shrine. The present [[Honden]] was made in [[1795]]. It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Business Japan|date=July 1988|publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun|language=en}} == Architecture == The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''. {{Infobox Chinese | kanji = 水若酢神社 | romaji = Mizuwakasu jinja | hiragana = みずわかすじんじゃ }} == Cultural Status == The shrine is designated as an [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government. == festivals == The grand festival is held on May 3 in odd-numbered years. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine has been located at its current site since 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. A white heron is said to have guided the deity to the present location, and a sacred pine tree called "Myōjin no Matsu" grew near the second torii gate until it died in 1971{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}. === Shrine Buildings === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, built in 1795, is an example of the [[Oki-zukuri]] style, unique to the region. The building is designated as an Important Cultural Property, along with associated documents{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. The worship hall, built in 1912, features a plaque inscribed with "First Shrine of Oki Province" from 1772{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. The gate was built in 1811{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. Other examples of Oki-zukuri include the main halls of [[Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine]] and [[Ise no Mikoto Shrine]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. File:Mizuwakasu-jinja suizhin-mon.jpg|Zuijin Gate File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ninotorii.jpg|Second Torii Gate === Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja kofun-1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumulus 1 Stone Chamber}}]] The shrine grounds contain several kofun (tumuli) from the Kofun period, known as the Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Only two tumuli remain today: :; Tumulus 1 :: Located east of the shrine buildings. The burial facility is a horizontal stone chamber with a total length of about 11 meters, the largest in the Oki Islands. Artifacts such as iron products and beads have been found{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. :; Tumulus 2 :: Located behind the shrine buildings. The details are unknown{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. == festivals == Major festivals at Mizuwakasu Shrine include{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=140-153}}: * New Year's Day festival (January 1) * Praying for Good Harvest (February 17) * '''festival''' (May 3) *: Known for the Sairei Furyu, a festival procession held every other year (even-numbered years). Events include the Yama-biki (Pulling the Mountain) ceremony, a procession of a decorated float called "Hōraisan," and various performances such as kagura, horseback archery, and dances. The festival is one of the "Three Great festivals of Oki" and is a designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. * Mid-year festival (June 16) * Harvest festival (November 3) * Gozasara festival (November 6) * Gozairi festival (December 6) * Year-End festival (December 31) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * main hall (with 8 wooden plaques and 6 construction documents) (Architecture) - Built in 1795. It is a ''[[Myojin Taisha]]''. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] [[Oki Province]] or the highest ranked shrine in the province.{{Cite web |title=Mizuwakasu Shrine {{!}} List of Geopark Sites and Treasures |url=https://www.oki-geopark.jp/en/geopark-sites-features-list/2694/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Oki Islands UNESCO Global Geopark |language=en-US}} It is ranked as a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a special shrine by the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The crest of the shrine has a chrysanthemum symbol.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-28 |title=水若酢神社（Mizuwakasu Shrine） - shrine-heritager |url=https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528184043/https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |archive-date=2023-05-28 }} It enshrines the deity Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto. This deity is linked to land development in Oki Province and sea protection.{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JSMvAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Shinto shrines and festivals |date=1958 |publisher=Association of Shinto Shrines, Kokugakuin University, Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics |language=ja}} == Overview == [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ichinotorii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii Gate}}]] '''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, Mizuwakasu Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]]. It is a [[Myōjin Taisha]] (Grand Shrine) of the [[Engishiki]], the [[Ichinomiya]] of [[Oki Province]], and a former [[Kokuhei Chūsha]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine under the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine's crest (kamon) is "Chrysanthemum" . == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following three deities Shrine history documentation.{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}: ; Main deity :* '''Mizuwakasu no Mikoto''' (水若酢命) ; Auxiliary Deities :* Nakagoto no Mikoto (中言命, Nakagoto Kami) :* Suzu no Gozen (鈴御前) === About the Deities === [[File:Tamawakasumikoto jinja Haiden.JPG|thumb|240px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine|ja|玉若酢命神社}} (Okinoshima-cho, Shimane)}}{{small|The Sōja (provincial shrine) of Oki Province. The connection between "Tamawakasu no Mikoto" and "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto" is noted.}}]] The deity's name in the [[Engishiki]] is recorded as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine." Although Mizuwakasu no Mikoto does not appear in major texts like the [[Kojiki]] or [[Nihon Shoki]], its origins are unclear due to the loss of historical documents in fires during the Middle Ages{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The meaning of "Mizu" can be interpreted as "water" or "auspicious," and "Wakasu" is also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The connection between this shrine and the nearby Tamawakasu no Mikoto Shrine is also noted{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. The origins of the auxiliary deities Nakagoto no Mikoto and Suzu no Gozen are also unclear{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. The traditional text "Imijuyuraki" mentions these deities{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=69-90}}. == History == === Founding === Most of the ancient documents regarding the shrine's history were lost during the Middle Ages. According to the "Oki Chronicles" (1688), the deity appeared from the sea during the reign of Emperor Sujin and moved to its current location following the white doves{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. Another document from 1795 mentions that the deity was enshrined during the reign of Emperor Nintoku{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. According to local tradition, the deity moved several times before settling in its current location in Koori village during the Edo period{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=57-68}}. The current site is thought to have been the ancient district office of the Oki Province, evidenced by the large-scale kofun (tumuli) in the area{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. === Historical Summary === ==== Ancient Period ==== In the [[Shoku Nihongi]] (842 AD), it is recorded that the shrine, along with two others, was granted official status{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. In the [[Engishiki]] (927 AD), the shrine is listed as "Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine, Myōjin Taisha"{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The area is identified as Kawauchi-go in the Onji District, based on the names in the [[Wamyō Ruijushō]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. There are no records of the shrine from the mid-Heian to the early 15th century{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. ==== Medieval Period ==== The first medieval reference is from 1429, noting the shrine as the "Grand Shrine of Oki"{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}. It is noted as the Ichinomiya of Oki Province from 1530{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}The Ichinomiya of Oki Province is sometimes identified as Yurahime Shrine, based on a note in the [[Dainihonkok Ichinomiya-ki]], but this is disputed by scholars{{Sfn|The Study of Medieval Provincial Shrines|2000|p=440}}.. In the medieval period, the Oki Province was ruled by the Oki clan, leading to conflicts and the fall of the shrine's head priests{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. ==== Early Modern Period ==== In the Edo period, the shrine was relocated in 1676 after a flood and rebuilt at its current location in 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. The main hall, built in 1795, is a designated Important Cultural Property{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. During the late Edo period, the shrine was involved in political movements, including the Sonnō Jōi (Revere the Emperor, Expel the Barbarians) movement{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Nihon Daijiten)|2000}}. ==== Modern Period ==== After the [[Meiji Restoration]], the shrine was designated as a Kokuhei Chūsha in 1871 and later registered as a Beppyo Shrine{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}. === Shrine ranking === * Senior Third rank (Engishiki) - Listed as "Mizuwakasu Myōjin." == History == According to legend, the deity rose from the sea, off the shore of Igo, crossed Mt. Ōmine and entered the former Goka Village. The shrine might date back to the Kofun Period. This was during [[Emperor Suinin|Emperor Suijin]] or [[Emperor Nintoku]]'s reign. In the [[Engishiki Jinmyocho]], it was listed as a [[Myojin Taisha]] in 927.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QmdRAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Engi-shiki; Procedures of the Engi Era: Books VI-X|date=1972|publisher=Sophia University|language=en}} The shrine is important in Oki Province. It guards the [[Sea of Japan]]. It appears in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', a historical text. The ''Inshū Shicho Gakki'', from the [[Edo Period]], mentions it. The {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|sv}} names it as Mizuwakasu Myojin Oki Ichinomiya Shrine. The present [[Honden]] was made in [[1795]]. It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu|title=Business Japan|date=July 1988|publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun|language=en}} == Architecture == The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''. {{Infobox Chinese | kanji = 水若酢神社 | romaji = Mizuwakasu jinja | hiragana = みずわかすじんじゃ }} == Cultural Status == The shrine is designated as an [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] by the Japanese government. == festivals == The grand festival is held on May 3 in odd-numbered years. == Shrine Grounds == The shrine has been located at its current site since 1678{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. A white heron is said to have guided the deity to the present location, and a sacred pine tree called "Myōjin no Matsu" grew near the second torii gate until it died in 1971{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=39-56}}. === Shrine Buildings === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|main hall (Important Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall, built in 1795, is an example of the [[Oki-zukuri]] style, unique to the region. The building is designated as an Important Cultural Property, along with associated documents{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. The worship hall, built in 1912, features a plaque inscribed with "First Shrine of Oki Province" from 1772{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. The gate was built in 1811{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=9-21}}. Other examples of Oki-zukuri include the main halls of [[Tamawakasu Mikoto Shrine]] and [[Ise no Mikoto Shrine]]{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=91-103}}. File:Mizuwakasu-jinja suizhin-mon.jpg|Zuijin Gate File:Mizuwakasu-jinja ninotorii.jpg|Second Torii Gate === Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli === [[File:Mizuwakasu-jinja kofun-1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumulus 1 Stone Chamber}}]] The shrine grounds contain several kofun (tumuli) from the Kofun period, known as the Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Only two tumuli remain today: :; Tumulus 1 :: Located east of the shrine buildings. The burial facility is a horizontal stone chamber with a total length of about 11 meters, the largest in the Oki Islands. Artifacts such as iron products and beads have been found{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. :; Tumulus 2 :: Located behind the shrine buildings. The details are unknown{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine Tumuli (Heibonsha)|1995}}. == festivals == Major festivals at Mizuwakasu Shrine include{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu Shrine (Student Publishing)|2005|pp=140-153}}: * New Year's Day festival (January 1) * Praying for Good Harvest (February 17) * '''festival''' (May 3) *: Known for the Sairei Furyu, a festival procession held every other year (even-numbered years). Events include the Yama-biki (Pulling the Mountain) ceremony, a procession of a decorated float called "Hōraisan," and various performances such as kagura, horseback archery, and dances. The festival is one of the "Three Great festivals of Oki" and is a designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Shimane Prefecture{{Sfn|Mizuwakasu no Mikoto Shrine (Engishiki)|1983}}Explanation board for Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu, set up by Okinoshima Town Education Committee.. * Mid-year festival (June 16) * Harvest festival (November 3) * Gozasara festival (November 6) * Gozairi festival (December 6) * Year-End festival (December 31) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * main hall (with 8 wooden plaques and 6 construction documents) (Architecture) - Built in 1795. Designated on January 21, 1992{{Cultural Heritage Database|102|2991|Mizuwakasu Shrine main hall}}. === Shimane Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Intangible Folk Cultural Property ** Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu - Designated on March 30, 1973[http://www.town.okinoshima.shimane.jp/www/contents/1001000000257/index.html Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties (Intangible Cultural Properties) > Mizuwakasu Shrine festival Furyu] (Okinoshima Town Education Committee).. == location == '''location''' * 723 Koori, Okinoshima-cho, Oki District, [[Shimane Prefecture]] '''Access''' * From [[Saigo Port]], take the [[Oki Ichibata Bus]] to "Mizuwakasu Shrine-mae" bus stop (about 40 minutes) - Very few buses operate.
